mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC fell back from -9.6 to -11.7 in the most recent week after a brief improvement, indicating momentum has reversed toward the deeper deficit regime seen two weeks prior. This short-term autocorrelation implies the decline will persist into the near term before any further stabilization.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC moved from -9.6 (t-1w) to -11.7 (t-0w), reversing the prior week's improvement
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 4-week forward mean is higher than its 4-week trailing mean despite the single-week reversal, the momentum-carryover mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility remains deeply suppressed around -30 points and tightened again from -28.1 to -30.0 in the latest week. When transit usage drops below -30 for consecutive weeks, it signals renewed commuter and shopper avoidance of crowded transit-linked retail corridors, pulling RETAIL_REC lower over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -30 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -28.1 (t-1w) to -30.0 (t-0w), crossing back below -30
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's next-2-week mean rises or stays flat despite TRANSIT remaining below -30 for two straight weeks, the threshold mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT jointly proxy the commuting-linked activity bundle that feeds adjacent retail and recreation trips. Even though each individually is modest, a simultaneous stabilization or mild recovery in both series over consecutive weeks compounds into a stronger lift for RETAIL_REC than either series could produce alone, because commuters combine transit trips with retail stops.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -8.6 to -7.6 between t-3w and t-2w while TRANSIT also improved from -31.1 to -28.1 by t-1w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 4-week forward mean fails to exceed its trailing mean even when both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT show simultaneous week-on-week improvement, the interaction hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility swung sharply from -9.1 to -20.9 in the latest week, consistent with a seasonal or weather-driven outdoor activity shift rather than policy change. In a seasonal regime where outdoor visits oscillate due to weather, a parks dip of this magnitude tends to be followed by compensatory indoor retail and recreation visits over the subsequent two weeks as people substitute indoor shopping for outdoor leisure.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped from -9.1 (t-1w) to -20.9 (t-0w), the largest weekly swing in the snapshot
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's next-2-week mean does not rise following the sharp PARKS decline, the seasonal substitution mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility moves inversely to RETAIL_REC across the snapshot (e.g., RESIDENTIAL rose from 2.9 to 3.6 while RETAIL_REC fell from -9.6 to -11.7). This persistent inverse coupling reflects a behavioral trade-off between staying home and going out; continued elevation in RESIDENTIAL mobility signals sustained caution that will keep RETAIL_REC depressed relative to its recent trailing mean, with eventual mean-reversion pulling RETAIL_REC back up as RESIDENTIAL stabilizes.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL and RETAIL_REC moved in opposite directions each week in the snapshot
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's forward 4-week mean remains below its trailing mean while RESIDENTIAL also declines over the same period, the inverse mean-reversion mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has stayed near baseline and even turned slightly positive at t-1w (0.7), indicating essential-activity restrictions have eased or remained loose. This policy-permissive backdrop for essential retail typically precedes a similar loosening for discretionary retail and recreation within the following week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM reached 0.7 at t-1w, its highest value in the snapshot
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 1-week forward value does not rise following GROCERY_PHARM's near-baseline or positive readings, the policy-spillover mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has not materially recovered, holding near -8.0 after a brief uptick to -7.6. When WORKPLACES declines or fails to improve by more than 0.5 points over two consecutive weeks, it signals weak commuter-driven foot traffic that depresses adjacent RETAIL_REC visits over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES fails to improve by more than 0.5 points over two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES moved from -7.6 (t-2w) to -7.9 (t-1w) to -8.0 (t-0w), a stagnating/worsening trend
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's next-2-week mean rises despite WORKPLACES stagnating or worsening, the commuter-linkage threshold hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of lockdown easing, PARKS and RESIDENTIAL together capture the balance between outdoor leisure seeking and home confinement. When PARKS volatility is high (large week-to-week swings) while RESIDENTIAL simultaneously trends downward, it indicates households are actively substituting varied outdoor and errand activities for home-bound time, which jointly lifts RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks beyond what either series alone would predict.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS swung from -16.9 to -9.1 then to -20.9 while RESIDENTIAL stayed near 3.0-3.9 with a dip to 2.9 at t-1w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's forward 4-week mean fails to exceed its trailing mean during periods of high PARKS volatility combined with declining RESIDENTIAL, the interaction hypothesis is rejected.
